issues.description: The problem specification (UML and text) defines checkOrderReady() with no parameters (checkOrderReady(): void), but the solution implements checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging) taking a boolean parameter. This parameter mismatch changes the required method signature and how orderMeal should call it (orderMeal is expected to call checkOrderReady() with no args). Students implementing the method as specified in the problem will produce a different signature than the solution, causing confusion and potential test mismatches.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the solution to implement checkOrderReady() with no parameters to match the problem statement. Update orderMeal to call checkOrderReady() without arguments. If the boolean flag is needed for debugging, implement an internal or private mechanism (e.g., a private field or separate debug method) instead of altering the required public signature.

issues.description: The problem specification (UML and text) defines a no-argument method checkOrderReady(): void on SealSaloon, but the provided solution implements checkOrderReady with a boolean parameter (checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging)). This changes the public method signature for the same conceptual operation and can confuse students mapping the requirement to the implementation (they will expect a no-arg method).
issues.suggestedFix: Provide a public no-argument checkOrderReady() method to match the problem statement (checkOrderReady(): void). If logging control is desired, keep an internal overloaded or private checkOrderReady(boolean) helper and have the public no-arg method call it (e.g., public void checkOrderReady() { checkOrderReady(true); }). This preserves the expected API while retaining internal logging functionality.
